02

THE IDEA

Precision that holds through motion.

Loco-manipulation asks more of a humanoid than reproducing a motion. Its hands must reach the right place, its feet must preserve support, and that accuracy must survive changes in posture and movement.

Anchor 1 follows sparse targets from human motion without online retargeting. Curated robot references guide whole-body coordination during training, while feedback corrects execution errors without changing the intended motion representation.

03

THE BENCHMARK

Benchmarking manipulation-oriented whole-body control.

Three complementary tracks assess manipulation-related coordination, general motion tracking, and target-based reaching.

A IN-HOUSE
15,342motions

Structured motion-capture tasks probe whole-body coordination across postures and locomotor conditions.

B PUBLIC
2,230motions

External motion datasets test tracking across broader motion sources and dynamic behaviors.

C REACHABILITY
3,210references

Prescribed wrist targets across five postures test sustained tracking and support stability.

04

Tracking precision, stability, and reachability in simulation

Tracking precision, task success and stable support across complementary experiments.

Data & evaluation notes＋

G / L denote reference-input modes, independently of the scoring frame. Motion success requires sustained tracking: wrist and ankle position errors ≤10 cm, orientation errors ≤1 rad, and other body-position errors ≤25 cm. Mean errors use frames before the first 25 cm body-position failure.

Reachability uses robot-space references and requires successful global tracking with no slips, unwanted steps, or touchdowns.

TELEOPERATION & AUTONOMY

Teleoperation and autonomous whole-body manipulation

A common sparse-reference interface connects different operators, capture devices, and higher-level policies to whole-body control.

Demonstration collection results＋

VISION · LANGUAGE · ACTION

Autonomous task execution with sparse and motion-token interfaces

Time progresses from left to right →

A vision-language-action policy predicts sparse body-part targets and hand commands. Anchor 1 executes the whole-body references in a closed loop. The architecture also supports a motion-token interface through reconstructed near-term targets.

Autonomous task success by interface＋

METHOD

Sparse human references and decoupled error feedback

Human motion specifies the targets. Curated robot motion guides coordination. Explicit error feedback supports precise execution.

ARCHON

Towards Whole-Body Intelligence

Alongside the release, we are preparing a community challenge around precise, stable whole-body control. We will announce the tracks, submission protocol, and schedule as they are finalized. Deployment feedback, shared evaluations, and new task requirements will help guide subsequent model and tooling updates.

Anchor 1 is one step in our broader effort toward whole-body intelligence. We hope this release gives others a useful starting point: a controller to build with, a benchmark to test against, and a concrete way to show where the next improvement is needed.

At Archon, we build whole-body intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. If you are interested in our mission, get in touch and join us! Other inquiries can be directed to contact@archon.tech.
